content.jointProblem: How can Lex Automatika insert robust Serbian Cyrillic–Latin transliteration and mixed-script normalisation into its PostgreSQL full-text search pipeline—at indexing time, query time, or both—so contract search retrieves documents across scripts without noticeable latency degradation, while resolving dialect-dependent mapping ambiguities?

rationale.text: Papp's doctoral and group focus is cross-lingual alignment in multilingual legal corpora, matching the legal-contract and cross-script setting.

sources.quote: dissertation on cross-lingual sentence alignment in multilingual legal corpora

rationale.text: She has direct transliteration and phonetic-normalisation experience in cross-lingual Serbian–Hungarian record matching.

sources.quote: using a combination of phonetic normalisation, transliteration, and fuzzy attribute matching

rationale.text: She has built fine-tuned multilingual transformer document matching across South Slavic languages without explicit translation.

sources.quote: identify semantically equivalent tender notices across Serbian, Croatian, and Macedonian without explicit translation

rationale.text: She has worked on incremental indexing and script normalisation for mixed-script Serbian news streams.

sources.quote: Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja.

rationale.text: She has prior industry experience deploying cross-lingual Serbian–Hungarian document matching.

sources.quote: automated cross-lingual matching of damage-claim documents submitted in Serbian and Hungarian

risks: Transfer gap: Papp's mixed-script real-time search work was evaluated on a simulated news stream, not on Lex Automatika's PostgreSQL contract index; the first experiment must test script-normalised search on the company's actual contract documents and query logs.
Dialect-dependent Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings may remain ambiguous without a company-approved mapping policy; this is explicitly acknowledged as an edge case in the task.
Papp is currently at full teaching load and can take on new projects only from late 2025 onward, which may not align with the company's six-week backend-engineer window.
The company has only one backend engineer available for up to six weeks, which may limit integration, reindexing and latency evaluation.
A robust solution must handle mixed-script documents, not only fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones, so simple query-time transliteration may be insufficient.
